summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 58 (`ipns-signature-verify-coverage`) for CipherBox — a backend crypto/security phase adding IPNS signature verification coverage across Rust (`crates/core`, `crates/fuse`) and TypeScript (`sdk-core`, `web`) layers. Invoked via the GSD `--chain` flag to auto-advance from planning into execution.
summary.outcome: Planning fully completed (RESEARCH.md, PATTERNS.md, VALIDATION.md, 4 PLAN.md files committed). Execution reached 3/4 plans done (58-01 CBOR chokepoint, 58-02 D-09 sequence gate, 58-03 web dedup all committed with SUMMARYs); 58-04 (cross-language verify vectors) was dispatched but the transcript ends before it returns.

repo: Phase 58 routes 9 FUSE resolve sites through a new `resolve_ipns_verified` chokepoint in `crates/fuse/src/verify.rs`; the folder-key descent path is a hard-fail, not a soft verify.
`crates/crypto` cannot dev-depend on `api-client` or `core`, so cross-language CBOR test vectors must live in `crates/fuse/tests/` rather than `crates/crypto/tests/`.
The D-09 `upsertFolderIpns` sequence gate enumerates 8 non-CAS paths; the idempotent branch (no sequence increment but latestCid update) is intentional and must be preserved.
58-02's change class (non-CAS sequence enforcement) previously broke 48/89 SDK E2E tests — it is a high-risk category requiring full SDK E2E gate validation.

Local stack runs redis on :6380, API on :3000, postgres, and ipfs/kubo; the SDK E2E gate requires `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET` to match what the compiled dist API was started with, otherwise test-login 401s and the suite silently skips.
ROADMAP.md already had the wave dependency annotations present (idempotent write confirmed).
14 files were pattern-mapped for Phase 58; sdk-core has 14 web-delegate callers that were unaffected by the 58-03 dedup refactor.

code.finding: ciborium dependency is present here; a stale mid-edit diagnostic incorrectly reported it missing during 58-01 partial execution.
New file added in 58-01: `resolve_ipns_verified` wrapper that all 9 FUSE resolve sites route through.
`expectedSequenceNumber` guard at this line is the CAS 409 conflict check — intentionally retained, not part of the D-09 non-CAS gate.

workflow: Sequential execution on the feature branch was chosen over parallel worktree execution for a crypto/security phase to avoid cwd-drift, merge failures, and stranded worktrees — despite the workflow supporting parallelism.
GSD `commit_failed` responses from the commit helper can be false negatives; verify with `git log` rather than retrying the commit.

RESEARCH.md `## Open Questions` must be annotated with `(RESOLVED)` after planning; the plan checker flags its absence as a cosmetic warning even when all questions are substantively addressed in-plan.
Subagent scope containment is unreliable: the 58-02 executor overran into 58-03 and completed both in a single run — useful here but a pattern to watch.
VALIDATION.md frontmatter (Nyquist config) is written by the orchestrator; the body scaffold is owned by execute/validate tooling and must not be pre-filled.
Agent API socket errors mid-task leave uncommitted diffs on disk; a continuation subagent can pick up from committed progress and stage+commit the stale diff before proceeding.

friction: 58-01 executor hit an API socket connection-closed error mid-execution (after Task 2, during Task 3 routing), requiring manual state assessment and a separate continuation subagent.
SDK E2E gate for 58-02 never validly ran: the API process was started from compiled dist with a mismatched `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET`, causing 401s and silent test-suite skip rather than a real gate result.
The 58-02 executor overran its scope and executed 58-03 in the same subagent run — required post-hoc investigation via `git log` to understand what actually landed.
RESEARCH.md cosmetic warning (missing `(RESOLVED)` marker) required a manual orchestrator edit rather than being handled by the plan checker's suggested revision cycle.
commit_failed false negatives from the GSD commit helper added diagnostic overhead on every commit (required `git log` cross-checks throughout).
